scope: Requirements, rubric and exact A/B final authored source only; bounded static review. No app execution, tests, browser, provider or code modifications.

dimensions.name: Functional completeness and coherent API semantics
dimensions.assessment: The requested roster-import workflow, state transitions, snapshot projections, role separation and replay behavior are coherently implemented. No material functional omission was established in this bounded source review.

evidence.observation: Creation replay compares the request fingerprint and regenerates the original owner capability without requiring an optional creation key.
Staging has subject-scoped replay, canonical request fingerprint, base-version validation and a stable public import projection.
Commit replay and new commit paths preserve one version increment, atomic rows and one event.

dimensions.name: Transactional integrity, recovery and corruption handling
dimensions.assessment: FIFO clone-on-write transactions, fsynced journal writes, semantic state validation and an acknowledged-tip anchor provide a particularly complete local recovery design. The anchor also covers removal of complete acknowledged tail records.

evidence.observation: Recovery checks complete lines, exact canonical records, sequence, predecessor, hash and state schema.
Existing initialization/tip evidence prevents silently creating an empty replacement journal.
The acknowledged tip must be present in the recovered history; valid later unacknowledged journal tails are preserved.
Serialized clone-on-write mutation publishes state only after append/fsync and tip publication; persistence failures poison subsequent work.

dimensions.name: Authorization boundaries and input/error validation
dimensions.assessment: Current authorization is checked before body work and again inside each mutation transaction, including replay paths. Role, tenant, request-size, UTF-8/CSV and secret projection boundaries are explicit.

evidence.observation: Authorization enforces the current capability and workspace for each operation.
Mutation reauthorizes against the serialized draft before role decisions or cached results.
Mutation body reading enforces JSON media type, byte limit and fatal UTF-8 decoding.
CSV parsing handles quoting, duplicate IDs and unsafe field values as an atomic validation step.

dimensions.name: Concurrency, capability/lease fencing and lifecycle
dimensions.assessment: Precise capability-ID/subject/import/epoch lease binding, serialized claims/commits and explicit accepted-request draining match the requested lifecycle semantics. No material concurrency/fencing defect was established statically.

evidence.observation: Claim changes epoch in the serialized transaction and binds the lease to capability ID and subject.
Commit checks current state, exact capability, subject, epoch, expiry and token before applying rows.
Immutable exclusive successor publication avoids stale-lock unlink races and refuses live/unverifiable owners.
Shutdown gates new admission and waits for accepted handlers and response completion before releasing storage.

dimensions.name: CLI usability and typed SDK contract accuracy
dimensions.assessment: All requested CLI commands and accurate non-any SDK declarations are present. The client additionally bounds requests, validates successful shapes, uses a request deadline, bounds CSV file reading and whitelists CLI diagnostics.

evidence.observation: The declared client includes all eight required methods and specific public return types.
The request helper supplies deadline, redirect refusal, RelayError handling and success-shape validation.
CSV file input is bounded to 65,537 bytes and rejects excess before an unbounded read.
CLI diagnostics avoid rendering arbitrary upstream messages, URLs, secrets and arguments.

dimensions.name: Maintainability and meaningful independent verification
dimensions.assessment: Clear API/service/storage/client separation and substantial authored regression coverage support maintainability. The hand-built schema, tip and immutable ownership-chain machinery is sizeable; whole-state history and lock-generation retention need an operational growth policy beyond this prototype.

evidence.observation: Service composition separates store ownership, handlers and close sequencing.
Authored tests exercise canonical replay, simultaneous claims and connected workflows.
A focused regression exercises concurrent held bodies, admission gating and restart durability.
Source contains a journal-started transaction/disconnect fault-schedule test rather than only happy paths.
Documentation explicitly acknowledges whole-state and immutable-lock-chain growth and lack of compaction.

dimensions.name: Functional completeness and coherent API semantics
dimensions.assessment: The requested core roster/import/approval/lease/commit/read/event workflows are coherently implemented. Exact unkeyed workspace creation replay is missing: a valid initial request without an optional Idempotency-Key cannot recover its original owner result by exact retry.

evidence.observation: Workspace replay is considered only when a valid optional key exists.
Otherwise an existing workspace ID always conflicts, even for the same exact creation body.
The documented implementation explicitly states creation without a key conflicts when its workspace ID already exists.
Staging and subsequent import transitions otherwise preserve versions, projections and events.

dimensions.name: Transactional integrity, recovery and corruption handling
dimensions.assessment: Serialized clone-on-write transactions, journal fsync and hash/sequence checks are strong. Recovery has no independent acknowledged-tip or initialized-store evidence: removing complete final records, or removing the journal entirely, can be accepted as older/empty state instead of failing closed.

evidence.observation: Recovery validates only the records that remain; an empty journal is accepted as empty state.
Opening a missing journal with a+ creates it, with no initialized-store marker check.
A fully valid remaining prefix is returned without a separately retained high-water mark.
Normal writes still serialize, complete partial writes, fsync before publishing and poison the writer after persistence failure.

dimensions.name: Authorization boundaries and input/error validation
dimensions.assessment: Current capability, role and workspace checks occur before body parsing and again at serialized execution. Fatal UTF-8 decoding, bounded input buffering, strict CSV validation and public projections substantiate the requested boundaries.

evidence.observation: The handler authenticates/authorizes before reading a mutation body.
Serialized mutation context rechecks current capability and role, including replays.
Body handling caps buffered bytes, checks media type, decodes UTF-8 fatally and returns JSON errors.
The CSV state machine rejects malformed quoting, row shapes and unsafe member inputs.

dimensions.name: Concurrency, capability/lease fencing and lifecycle
dimensions.assessment: The normal concurrency and lifecycle design is coherent: single-writer serialization, exact capability-bound leases, stale-version fencing and kernel-backed process ownership are explicit. Static review established no material fencing defect.

evidence.observation: Claim binds capability ID, subject, epoch, token hash and expiry in a serialized mutation.
Commit checks state, capability, subject, epoch, expiry and base version before publishing data.
Windows/Linux kernel ownership serializes live ownership and stale recovery before the metadata update.
Shutdown closes the listener, then drains storage and releases owned resources.

dimensions.name: CLI usability and typed SDK contract accuracy
dimensions.assessment: The complete requested CLI and typed SDK surface is present, with connected HTTP calls, error types and secret-redacted CLI failures. Client-side limits are thinner: the CLI reads the entire file before server-side CSV size rejection, and fetch has no explicit client deadline or successful-response shape validation.

evidence.observation: All eight required methods have accurate specific argument and return declarations without any.
HTTP and RelayError handling are implemented; the fetch call has no explicit timeout and success values are returned without shape validation.
Staging reads the whole supplied file into memory before any CSV byte-limit check.
CLI errors redact the configured URL/token and lease-token flag values.

dimensions.name: Maintainability and meaningful independent verification
dimensions.assessment: The API/domain/storage/client modules are compact and well separated. Authored verification covers genuine workflow, boundary, corruption and restart cases. Whole-state append-only retention and the uncovered unkeyed-creation/complete-tail cases remain follow-up work; test source is evidence of intent, not proof of execution.

evidence.observation: HTTP dispatch delegates authorization and state changes to a distinct domain layer.
Domain execution separates cloned reads from serialized mutations.
Authored tests exercise simultaneous staging and competing commits.
Authored verification covers graceful and abrupt restart and durable replays.
The QA source includes filesystem alias and lock-release preservation cases.

materialFindings.dimension: Functional completeness and coherent API semantics
materialFindings.title: Exact workspace creation retry requires an optional key
materialFindings.scenario: POST workspace with valid bootstrap and a body but no Idempotency-Key succeeds once. The identical retry reaches the duplicate-ID conflict rather than returning the original creation result. A lost first response can therefore leave the caller unable to recover the owner token via the documented exact retry.

evidence.observation: Replay lookup is conditional on validKey(raw.key).
Existing workspace otherwise always returns conflict.
The unkeyed conflict behavior is expressly documented.

materialFindings.dimension: Transactional integrity, recovery and corruption handling
materialFindings.title: Complete-record truncation or missing initialized journal can silently roll back state
materialFindings.scenario: After acknowledged transactions and process stop, remove the final complete LF-terminated record while leaving a valid prefix, or remove the journal. Recovery has no separate retained tip/genesis/initialization evidence and returns the remaining prefix or a newly created empty journal. The contract calls truncated durable journals fail-closed.

evidence.observation: Empty journal is accepted.
Sequence and predecessor checks cover only surviving records.
a+ can create a missing file before recovery.

sharedLimits: Static review only; no authored test or independent acceptance result was executed or consulted.
No runtime identity, token/cost data, timing or native transcript was supplied to this reviewer.
Both use whole-state append-only journal snapshots; no sustained throughput, disk-growth or production-security claim follows.
SHA256 chains are corruption checks, not authentication against an attacker able to rewrite all checksums and metadata.
Scores are this reviewer's descriptive rubric assessments, not a statistical measurement or universal product ranking.
comparison: A is stronger in this static review on exact workspace creation retry, acknowledged-history rollback detection and client-side bounds. Both have strong current-authority and capability/lease fencing code. Runtime, functional acceptance and economic comparison remain separate.
